## About this guide

> Create a report and graph from the snapshot used in [Getting started](atlas.html).

## Render the atlas

The report shows columns, foreign key dependencies and reverse usages. Pandoc builds the HTML and graph.

```{r report}
# Load the report and model functions.
library(db.atlas)
# Locate the installed example snapshot.
metadata_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", "metadata", package = "db.atlas")
# Build a model for the example database.
schema_model <- build_schema_model(read_metadata(metadata_directory))
# Write the example output to a temporary directory.
report_directory <- withr::local_tempdir()
# Configure the title and use stable filenames.
report_configuration <- atlas_report_config(
  title = "Survey database",
  output_directory = report_directory,
  timestamp_format = ""
)
# Generate the HTML report and dependency graph.
report_path <- render_schema_report(schema_model, report_configuration)
# Generate the report indexes.
generate_report_indexes(report_directory)
# List the HTML files created by the example.
list.files(dirname(report_path), pattern = "[.]html$")
```

## Customize the report

Set schema labels and colors in the configuration passed to `render_schema_report()`.

```{r report-options}
# Assign labels and colors to the example schemas.
report_configuration <- atlas_report_config(
  title = "Survey database",
  output_directory = report_directory,
  schemas = c("survey", "catalogue"),
  domain_labels = c(survey = "Survey records", catalogue = "Reference catalogue"),
  schema_colors = c(survey = "#2563EB", catalogue = "#D97706")
)
```

Use `logo`, `analytics_html` and `template_overrides` in `atlas_report_config()` for application-specific presentation.

The default templates and assets are available in [Package resources](resources.html).
